title: Why interfaces gained default, static, and private methods
answer: Default methods let an interface evolve with inheritable behavior; static methods let it host contract-related utilities; private methods let multiple default or static methods share internal implementation without exposing that helper as part of the public API. Together they improve interface evolution and organization while preserving the interface's primary role as a contract.
